title: WISEDRAM: A Reliable Bitwise In-DRAM Accelerator
problem: Processing-in-Memory (PIM) techniques in DRAM suffer from vulnerability to process variation and noise, internal cell leakage, and high latency in cell access, limiting real-world deployment of in-DRAM compute.
motivation: The enormous capacity, wide activation during cell access, and maturity of DRAM technology make it attractive for PIM, but reliability and latency challenges prevent practical adoption for complex workloads.
method: WISEDRAM uses one row of special X-cells to perform bitwise operations (AND, OR, XOR—combining data bits) directly in DRAM, while keeping all normal data reads and writes identical to standard DRAM procedures. This separation—computation in special cells, storage in normal cells—preserves DRAM's reliability while enabling parallel in-DRAM computation.
key_novelty: WISEDRAM is the first system to enable in-DRAM bitwise operations while keeping the conventional DRAM cell access procedures unchanged, preserving the reliability of standard DRAM.
contributions: Novel X-cell architecture for reliable in-DRAM bitwise operations
22% reduction in average bitwise computation latency vs. prior PIM approaches
71% improvement in XOR operation execution speed
Only 1.6% area overhead while maintaining standard DRAM reliability
primary_theme: Reliable in-DRAM bitwise accelerator leveraging X-cells
